name: Suitcase Carry
summary: A unilateral loaded carry where a single weight is held at one side while walking to build anti-lateral flexion core strength and grip endurance.

setup: Place a single heavy dumbbell or kettlebell on the floor beside one foot.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back to grip the handle firmly with one hand.
Stand fully upright, squaring your shoulders and hips so your torso remains completely vertical.
steps: Brace your core and begin walking forward with controlled, deliberate strides.
Keep the weight slightly off your thigh without leaning away from or toward the loaded side.
Maintain a tall posture and level shoulder line throughout the path.
Turn smoothly or stop after the target distance, lower the weight safely using a hip hinge, and repeat on the opposite side.
instructions.breathing: Maintain continuous, shallow diaphragmatic breathing behind a firmly braced abdominal wall throughout the walk.
cues: Keep shoulders level like a balance scale
Walk tall and don't let the weight drag you down

common_faults.fault: Leaning the torso away from the weight to compensate for the load.
common_faults.correction: Reduce the load and focus on maintaining a perfectly upright, vertical spine as if balancing a book on your head.

common_faults.fault: Resting the implement against the thigh during the walk.
common_faults.correction: Hold the working arm just far enough from the body to clear the hip, forcing the core to stabilize the load.

common_faults.fault: Rushing forward with choppy, unstable strides.
common_faults.correction: Slow your pace to a controlled, heel-to-toe gait to maximize time under tension and balance.

precautions: Ensure the walking pathway is completely free of tripping hazards.
Always lift and set down the weight using a proper hip hinge to protect your lower back.
